title: Product PRD: Unified Inference v15 — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:

This document captures the product requirements, high-level design, roadmap, pricing and packaging changes, and release notes for Unified Inference v15 (UI-v15). UI-v15 is the next major release of Redwood's Unified Inference platform focusing on predictable latency for multi-tenant workloads, expanded model variant routing, and a simplified pricing tier for mid-market customers.

Goals and Non-Goals:

- Goals:
  - Reduce 95th-percentile tenant latency by 20% for inference calls under 1s SLA across hosted and dedicated modes.
  - Introduce model-variant automatic fallback with per-customer policy controls.
  - Launch a new Mid-Market pricing tier that simplifies dedicated capacity commitments and adds an automated cost-saver profile.
  - Provide first-class observability for cost-per-token and quality regressions (prompt-set tied).
- Non-Goals:
  - Full rework of serving runtime internals (optimizations will be staged, but runtime ABI remains stable).

Success Metrics (KPIs):

- Performance: 95th percentile latency improvement of >=20% for targeted tenants (measured over a 30-day window).
- Reliability: Error rate <= 0.5% for inference API requests in Hosted mode (rolling 7d).
- Economics: Average cost-per-inference token reduced by >=10% for customers enabling the new cost-saver profile.
- Adoption: 25% of existing Dedicated customers migrated to the Mid-Market tier or enabled cost-saver profile within 90 days of GA.

User Personas and Primary Use Cases:

- Product/ML Engineers: Require predictable latency and fallback behavior for mission-critical chat and generation features.
- Platform/Infra Teams: Need clear capacity commitments and autoscaling controls for multi-region deployments.
- Finance/BizOps: Want simpler pricing tiers and transparent per-route cost breakdowns.

Scope and Requirements:

1) Functional Requirements:
- FR-001: Per-tenant Model Variant Routing. Customers can configure an ordered list of compatible model variants with weights and fallback priorities.
- FR-002: Automatic Fallback Policies. When primary model latency or errors exceed thresholds, requests should be routed to configured fallback variants within 50ms of detection.
- FR-003: Cost-Saver Profile. A profile customers can opt into that enables: conservative batching, prefix-KV cache retention heuristics, and quantization-first model selection where quality checks pass.
- FR-004: Observability: New dashboards exposing per-route cost-per-token, 95/99 latency, and prompt-set quality regression flags.
- FR-005: Migration API: Tools/endpoints for migrating Dedicated capacity commitments into the Mid-Market tier with minimal downtime.

2) Non-functional Requirements:
- NFR-001: Backward compatibility with existing SDKs and REST API for 12 months.
- NFR-002: SLOs: Hosted API availability >= 99.95% for GA tenants.
- NFR-003: Security: All routing decisions and audit events must be logged to tenant audit logs and retained per default retention policies.
- NFR-004: Performance: Fallback routing decision must add <=50ms median extra latency when invoked.

Design Overview (High-level):

- Routing Layer Changes:
  - Add a lightweight policy engine in the request path that evaluates tenant-specific routing rules (policies stored in config-proxy + cached in the inference edge).
  - Integrate health signals (per-node latency/error metrics) streamed from the serving runtime to the routing engine via the routing pub/sub channel.

- Fallback Execution:
  - When a threshold breach is detected, the routing engine marks the primary variant and triggers an immediate route to the next compatible variant. The runtime will attach a metadata header (X-RW-Fallback-Reason) for observability.

- Cost-Saver Profile Implementation:
  - Default conservative batcher params: max_batch_size = 8, max_wait_ms = 25 for interactive workloads.
  - KV cache TTL heuristics: adaptive retention based on token-reuse score; persistent cache for top-5 prefixes per tenant.
  - Quantization selection: runtime chooses INT8 variant when recent eval pass rate for key prompt-sets >= 98%.

Architecture & Components (textual diagram):

- Client -> API Gateway -> Routing Engine (policy cache, health signals) -> Serving Runtime Pool (primary/fallback variants) -> KV Cache Layer -> Response

- Supporting components: config-proxy (policy storage), telemetry-collector (health signals), cost-aggregator (per-route cost calculation), migration-service (capacity conversion flows).

Operational Playbook (Rollout & Rollback):

1) Canary Phase (2 weeks):
  - Select 3 low-risk tenants and 5 internal tenants. Enable routing engine and cost-saver profile with telemetry-only mode for 48 hours.
  - Step 1: Telemetry-only for 48h -> monitor 95/99 latency, error spikes, cost deltas.
  - Step 2: Enable fallback ON for canary tenants -> monitor fallback frequency and user impact (quality regression metrics).
2) Gradual Ramp (4 weeks):
  - Expand to 20% of tenants by traffic using auto-join rules (start with low-variance workloads).
  - Weekly checkpoints with product, infra, and SRE sign-off to proceed.
3) GA Launch:
  - Open opt-in for all tenants. Announce Mid-Market tier availability and pricing changes.

Rollback Criteria:

- If canary tenants show >3x baseline error rate or >30% increase in support tickets labelled "generation-quality" during the canary window, rollback to previous routing behavior within 1 hour.

Migration Strategy for Dedicated Customers to Mid-Market Tier:

- Migration API flow:
  1. Customer submits migration request via Console or API: desired new monthly commit and preferred regions.
  2. Migration service evaluates compatibility and estimates carbon of savings and suggested commit.
  3. A scheduled cutover window is proposed; Dedicated capacity is converted to a Mid-Market reservation with a temporary dual-commit period (up to 30 days) to avoid capacity churn.
  4. Post-migration monitoring and automatic adjustments to autoscaling policies.

Pricing & Packaging Notes:

- New Mid-Market Tier (target: SMBs and mid-market SaaS)
  - Monthly commit: $2,000 / month minimum (elastic commit options available).
  - Included: guaranteed baseline throughput (100k tokens/day), priority routing to regional pools, mid-market support SLA (4h).
  - Add-ons: Advanced observability retention, compliance pack, and premium SLA.

- Cost-Saver Profile: free opt-in for all tiers; potential 5-15% cost reduction estimated for typical chat workloads.

- Pricing migration credits: Customers who convert a Dedicated annual commit to Mid-Market within the first 60 days receive prorated credits equal to 10% of remaining commit value.

Backwards Compatibility & Deprecation Plan:

- The current dedicated-only fallback config will be supported and mapped to the new policy model automatically.
- Deprecated endpoints (legacy /v1/fallback) will be maintained for 12 months with a deprecation notice and SDK updates.

Developer and SDK Changes:

- SDK v6.3: adds client-side hints for routing preference and a new header to supply tenant prompt-sets for quality monitoring.
- REST API additions: POST /v2/tenants/{id}/routing-policy, GET /v2/tenants/{id}/cost-breakdown

Example: routing policy payload (YAML):

  routing_policy:
    primary: "redwood/gpt-5-xl"
    fallbacks:
      - variant: "redwood/gpt-5-lr-quant"
        weight: 70
      - variant: "redwood/gpt-5-medium"
        weight: 30
    thresholds:
      latency_ms: 800
      error_rate_pct: 1.0

Example curl (enable cost-saver for tenant):

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/tenants/1234/profiles/cost-saver -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"enabled": true}'

Release Notes (v15.0 — GA):

- Features:
  - Per-tenant model-variant routing with ordered fallback policies (FR-001 completed).
  - Cost-Saver profile with adaptive batching, KV heuristics, and quantization-first selection (FR-003 completed).
  - New Mid-Market pricing tier and migration credits for Dedicated customers.
  - Observability dashboards: per-route cost, prompt-set regression flags, and fallback traces (FR-004 completed).
- Fixes & Improvements:
  - Reduced median fallback decision latency from 120ms to 45ms in internal benchmarks.
  - Improved prefix cache eviction policy to reduce cold-start tokens by ~12%.
  - SDK updates to v6.3: client-side routing hints and prompt-set metadata support.
- Known Issues:
  - Edge case: certain long-sequence workloads may see higher quantization-induced quality variance; recommendation: disable quantization in cost-saver profile for those tenant routes.
  - Migration UI: initial console flow requires manual support approval in some edge regions.

Monitoring and SLOs (what to watch post-GA):

- Dashboards:
  - Per-tenant 95/99 latency and fallback frequency.
  - Per-route cost-per-token trend (7/30/90 day).
  - Prompt-set quality regression alerts (integrated with eval-harness).
- Alerting thresholds:
  - Fallback frequency > 2% for high-volume tenants -> P1 investigation.
  - 95th latency increase > 20% from baseline -> P1.
  - Cost-per-token increase > 30% after enabling cost-saver -> investigate auto-tuning regressions.

Appendix: Evaluation Criteria for Quantized Variants:

- For each tenant, run prompt-set evaluation of top-100 prompts. Accept quantized variant if BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval score >= 99% of baseline median over 3 runs.
